quarterly_data.signal: CEO Satish Dhanasekaran on wireless and 6G: wireless orders 'grew significantly again this quarter with rising customer investment in next-generation connectivity and continued demand across the supply chain supporting AI infrastructure scaling'. 'In June, the 3GPP plenary meeting in Singapore confirmed the timeline for 6G with the industry's first standard targeted for March 2029. With that milestone now set, customers are transitioning from exploratory research into funded development programs.' He names three emerging 6G technology areas - AI-RAN, integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) and non-terrestrial networks (NTN) - and says Keysight's portfolio 'is helping us secure early wins with industry leaders'. CEO view: 'our base case is the opportunity in 6G is greater than the opportunity that we saw in 5G, and we're well positioned to capitalize on it.'

CEO Satish Dhanasekaran on aerospace, defense and government: orders 'were up double digits with growth across all regions, driven by a heightened global focus on deterrence and defense modernization'. The shift to advanced radar architectures is 'leading to rapid adoption of our multichannel RF solutions and next-generation oscilloscopes at prime contractors'; engagements with defense startups and neo-primes are scaling, and 'this year, we achieved key wins across satellite, UAV, and phased array radar applications'; demand accelerated for Spirent's PNT (positioning, navigation and timing) solutions that emulate jamming and spoofing scenarios. In the Q&A: 'the demand from our prime contractors in aerospace defense remains strong as they're building out capacity. Sovereign investments in Europe is another tailwind for our defense business.' CEO view: 'we see a durable multi-year demand cycle ahead'. On the segment's slower revenue growth, CFO Neil Dougherty: 'we're still up double digits. There is some quarter-to-quarter perturbations in these end markets.'

AI demand in wireline, per CEO Satish Dhanasekaran: asked whether the run rate of the AI business within wireline was consistent with the prior quarter, he answered 'It has expanded.' He said the company was 'even stronger this quarter for our AI and wireline opportunities in Q3, and the pipeline continues to grow strongly', and 'we are in the early stages of a long adoption of AI, not just in wireline'. He sees a convergence into other end markets: AI is entering the RAN, and the wireless ecosystem's contract manufacturing companies 'have now started to invest in building their own racks for AI'. CSG President Kailash Narayanan: 'we're seeing R&D as well as our manufacturing business grow significantly.' CEO: 'we're also happy that we're participating in the volume part of the data center build-out as well.'
quarterly_data.figure: AI business run rate within wireline expanded vs the prior quarter

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Satish Dhanasekaran on the fiscal 2027 setup: 'we have no doubt a strong setup as we enter fiscal 2027, even as we remain cognizant of the outperformance you are seeing in 2026 on top of the growth year in 2025.' Product refresh: 'We just had the biggest refresh of our core RF microwave and high-speed digital products since we formed Keysight', reinforced at the worldwide annual sales training event in June, where the entire sales team was trained on this portfolio and the Spirent products; R&D investment made in the downturn 'has already started, a good refresh cycle for our new products, which are already being enthusiastically received by our customers'. CEO: 'I expect this to be a strong tailwind for us for many years'. Silicon designers are adopting Keysight's recently introduced high-performance digital and RF solutions for the lab.
quarterly_data.figure: biggest refresh of core RF microwave and high-speed digital products since Keysight was formed

quarterly_data.signal: Mix and profitability. CFO Neil Dougherty: 'we are on track to achieve record operating cash flow in fiscal 2026'. Software and services, per CEO Satish Dhanasekaran: 'we have trended as high as 40% a year or so ago, and now we are at 33%', at record levels in dollars; CFO: software and services are growing double digits, 'just not growing as fast as the hardware business is at this point in time'. EISG President Jason Kary: over the last 12-18 months the group focused on driving top-line growth and transforming pieces of the business - investing more in software elements with ESI and the Optical Solutions Group, rationalizing certain lower-margin pieces, and pursuing digital health and the grid; 'we're confident of our ability to continue to achieve higher levels of profitability as we move forward.' CEO: digital health was up double digits across wearables and monitoring, and education growth was supported by semiconductor workforce development solutions, particularly in Asia.
quarterly_data.figure: software and services 33% of revenue (as high as 40% a year or so ago)
